CHROMIUM: arm64: dts: mt8173-oak: add gpu nodes Add board node to enable gpu, and configure its power-supply. Different oak revisions have slightly different requirements: oak-rev0-2: uses MT8173-C which supports up to 494 MHz uses da9211 as its power-supply This patch also allows powering off this supply (ie when the GPU is off) oak-rev3 (the default) uses mt6397. uses MT8173-B which only supports up to 455 MHz uses mt6397 as its power-supply chromeos-4.4: This is a squash of the following commits from chromeos-3.18, moved later in the patch set (after first applying all upstream .dts node changes): 2d3be0bae521 CHROMIUM: arm64: dts: mt8173: Update GPU OPPs for oak-rev5 90d1f83d6296 [*] CHROMIUM: arm64: dts: mt8173-oak: Add oak-rev5 dts file 59f86979e68b CHROMIUM: arm64: dts: mt8173-oak: add gpu nodes [*] the hunk that moved the oak.dtsi gpu regulator (ie the default) from mt6397 -> da9211, and explicitly sets mt6396 for oak-rev3 & oak-rev4. Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Chiawen Lee <chiawen.lee@mediatek.com> BUG=chrome-os-partner:60805 TEST=build chromeos-4.4 for elm and boot TEST=build chromeos-4.4 for kevin and boot BUG=chrome-os-partner:40578 BUG=chrome-os-partner:45469 TEST=build and boot to UI on oak-rev3 & oak-rev2 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/269934 Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org> Change-Id: I76e12c12e9cf53d96569c5b5ac33fb7ad777e87b Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/423510 Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: drm/bridge: ps8640: Add a 3 ms delay before unmuting output For current ps8640 firmware, the PS_GPIO9 signal only indicates the bridge has seen the attached panel's HPD signal and read its EDID. Unfortunately, the bridge may not yet be ready to properly handle DSI/eDP traffic yet. For now, Paradetech has recommended adding a 3 ms delay after PS_GPIO9 before starting video signal transmission. Signed-off-by: Jitao Shi <jitao.shi@mediatek.com> Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> BUG=chrome-os-partner:53825 TEST=boot to ui on elm TEST=press reset button on debug board after show ui to boot on. => Can show ui everytime. TEST=Use magnet over F1 to repeatedly trigger lid close/open events Note: magnet must stay over magnet for ~0.5 to avoid triggering crbug.com/620208 => display comes on every time Change-Id: I9b252cbecea37adcd67a072280b73ca5a61bcf26 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/352943 Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: cawa cheng <cawa.cheng@mediatek.com> Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: jitao shi <jitao.shi@mediatek.com> Reviewed-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: jitao shi <jitao.shi@mediatek.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/423896 Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: drm/bridge: ps8640: Use individual regulators instead of bulk According to the latest information from Parade, the PS8640 1.2 V supply must be enabled before 3.3 V. So, split the bulk regulator into separate individual regulators that can be enabled independently. Signed-off-by: Jitao Shi <jitao.shi@mediatek.com> TEST=boot to ui on elm BUG=chrome-os-partner:57392 Change-Id: I9b48dfa45f61f45a58761f082558ad2feaa3182d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/411582 Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/423999 Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: drm/bridge: ps8640: add 5ms delay between v12 and v33 According to Parade, the PS8640 1.2V must be enabled 5 ms before its 3.3V. Otherwise, the PS8650 MCU may hang, and its settings cannot be written correctly, leading to a black screen. TEST=boot to ui on elm TEST=scope 5ms delay between 1.2v and 3.3v BUG=chrome-os-partner:57392 Change-Id: Ieeea9b19f10d52037889507e478215e242f84005 Signed-off-by: Jitao Shi <jitao.shi@mediatek.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/397018 Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/424000 Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: arm64: dts: mt8173-oak/-elm: Add internal display nodes Add nodes for the internal display pipe on the oak boards: mipi, dsi, bridge and panel nodes oak-rev5 is the current default. oak-rev2+ has a Parade PS8640 DSI-eDP on i2c4. For oak-rev2/3 & 5, the ps8650_fixed_1v2 uses gpio 30. oak-rev4 uses gpio 89. This fixed regulator actually takes 2 ms to ramp up when enabled. If we don't wait for the regulator to settle and take the PS8640 out of reset too early, sometimes the bridge will fail to start properly, and the eDP panel will stay black. UPSTREAM: PCI: rockchip: Fix rockchip_pcie_probe() error path to free resource list rockchip_pcie_probe() calls of_pci_get_host_bridge_resources() to parse resources from DT and build a resource list. The caller is responsible for disposing of the resource list. This is normally done by pci_release_host_bridge_dev() when the host bridge is removed. If the host bridge probe fails, dispose of the resource list in the probe error path. [bhelgaas: changelog] Suggested-by: Bjorn Helgaas <bhelgaas@google.com> Signed-off-by: Shawn Lin <shawn.lin@rock-chips.com> Signed-off-by: Bjorn Helgaas <bhelgaas@google.com> (cherry picked from commit f1d722b607d610b66785f7f00d2e1d457260647c) Conflicts: drivers/pci/host/pcie-rockchip.c BUG=b:36043263 TEST=build and boot Change-Id: I0ec17753b77ba8deabbb1d55d59ab318369c3bcb Signed-off-by: Jeffy Chen <jeffy.chen@rock-chips.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/451163 Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: PCI: rockchip: Set vendor ID from local core config space The TRM says the vendor ID in the RC's configure space can be rewritten and the value must be the same as the value read from the local core configure space.
